topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the scope of the material to be covered.

topics.label: Innate recognition of infection and tissue damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immune cells detect microbial infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns and pattern recognition receptor signaling cascades.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells prompt endothelial adhesion and chemokine gradients to recruit circulating leukocytes into inflamed tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells migrate through the lymphatic vasculature to lymph nodes to initiate adaptive immune responses.

topics.label: Pathology and mortality of septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the clinical dangers and physiological consequences of excessive systemic cytokine release.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and establish chronic inflammatory states such as granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the subject of the next lecture.
